request.state: We are assigning a new implementation effort for a departmental business language written by AI agents. The product priorities are adoption, token economy, visible company decisions and a single standard route for operations. Repository inspection found only an initial Rust CLI, a Python grammar experiment and a syntax-coloring editor extension; the 39 source apps and 21 handwritten JavaScript targets do not yet run. Production output must be JavaScript on workerd, with TypeScript implementation of the libraries and imports named @canlang/stdlib and @canlang/ui. Existing web facilities, Cloudflare resources, Wrangler and appropriate third-party packages should supply their existing functionality. There will be exactly five user-started Muse leads. Each works in its own Git worktree, delegates files to agents inside that same checkout, and repeats small PR, self-review, validation and merge cycles. Additional orchestrators and child worktrees are excluded. We need balanced useful effort and nonoverlapping ownership, including an early real end-to-end result; throughput estimates are unmeasured. Scope includes parser/name/type/composition analysis; code generation and IR; IDE/LSP/formatter/lints; scalar semantics, queries and protected transactions; asynchronous dispatch/timers/files/adapters; login/team identity, UI/localization and MCP; deployment/build/local runs, upgrades, BDD execution and release qualification. The approved D1 design combines an optimistic revision assertion with an atomic batch; every writer participates. History/fanout candidate syntax has no approval and must not silently become executable. Partition A gives lead1 compiler and every Rust/editor authoring tool, lead2 core values/queries/state/stdlib, lead3 durable execution/providers/file lifecycle, lead4 identity/web/i18n/MCP, and lead5 platform assembly/deploy/migration coordination/dev/test runner/integration/releases. One team controls Rust semantics but also carries all authoring features; the fifth lead needs meaningful early integration work. Partition B gives lead1 language analysis and JS emission, lead2 lint/format/LSP/editor/agent feedback, lead3 core state/stdlib plus identity, lead4 asynchronous work/providers/files, and lead5 web/MCP plus platform delivery/dev/test execution/qualification. Its dedicated authoring team can progress alongside parsing once analysis contracts exist; browser and deployment integration then concentrate in the fifth lead. In either arrangement production parsing, authority and commit behavior have exactly one implementation. A small shared contract milestone and producer-owned fixtures permit early parallel tests; mock-backed results cannot certify integrated behavior. Give shared workspace manifests and lockfiles a sole owner. Assess the same complete feature set and uncertainty for both partitions.

partition.instructions: Select the preferable initial division of the full implementation, weighing ownership interfaces and roughly balanced useful work with the stated uncertainty.

criteria.A: A places all language tooling with the compiler, separates core state and durable services, combines identity with user interfaces, and reserves a delivery/integration lead.
criteria.B: B creates a dedicated authoring-tools lane, joins identity to core execution, preserves a durable-services lane, and combines browser/MCP with delivery and integration.
